dialogue.Introduction: Name's Goblin Tinkerer. Used to be a goblin, back when I went around stealing shiny things from the adventurers. Now I fix things instead. Hot metal, sharp tongs, no more sneaking. You look like someone who breaks things, @.$h
dialogue.Mon: Morning, @. The forge was cold when I walked in, and a cold forge is a crime against iron. Something is always waiting to be heated around here.
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday. I like Tuesdays. Nobody comes in on Tuesdays wanting a sword sharpened in five minutes.$h
dialogue.Wed: I have a gizmo half built on the workbench. It has three springs and a little bit of cursed goblin magic. Don't touch it, @.
dialogue.Thu: The Mechanic keeps sending me wires to fix. I fix them, she sends more. I think that is called friendship.$h
dialogue.Fri: The Steampunker wants a gear on everything. Everything, @. My anvil has a gear on it now, and it turns. Don't ask.$u
dialogue.Sat: Market day. Half of Pelican Town comes by to see what I can squeeze out of old scrap. Last week I turned a rusty pan into a lantern.$h
dialogue.Sun: Sundays I clean the forge. Hot coals, sooty tongs, a lot of swearing. Peaceful, really.
dialogue.Mon4: You know, @, back when I was a goblin I only stole things and ran. Working the forge with people is much nicer. Thanks for stopping by.$h#$b#Don't tell the Merchant I said that. He'd try to charge me for it.
dialogue.Tue4: Every time someone brings me something broken, I feel a little like a healer. A healer for machines. And I charge double.$h
dialogue.Wed4: The old goblin armies made me build traps. Now I build pulleys and water wheels for the farms. Honestly, the farms are a far better hobby.$h
dialogue.Thu4: The Demolitionist once asked me for dynamite that could knock a hole in the moon. I said no, but I did make him a very nice fuse.$u
dialogue.Fri4: Whenever someone asks what I want to be when I grow up, I say a tinkerer. I was always going to be one, goblin or not.$h
dialogue.Sat4: I like your company at the saloon, @. The Tavernkeep pours a decent cider and never asks what I am doing with all the scrap in my pockets.$h
dialogue.Sun4: On quiet Sundays I think about the mines. All that metal down there. Sometimes I dream I am pulling a gear out of a rock. Strange, huh?$s
dialogue.Mon8: I'll be honest with you, @. When I first came to the valley I was sure everyone would remember the goblin in me. You never once looked at me that way.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Some nights I don't sleep well. The old goblin camps creep into my head. Being here in the forge with you makes the noise quieter.$s
dialogue.Wed8: If you ever need a bomb, a gadget or some fancy doohickey, you come to me first. I'd build you almost anything, @.$l
dialogue.Thu8: The Nurse says I should take breaks. I say the forge is my break. She says that is not how breaks work. She's usually right, which is annoying.$h
dialogue.Fri8: Every piece of scrap in this forge has a story behind it. I could tell you each one, @. Maybe I will, over a drink at the saloon.$l
dialogue.Sat8: Do you know the best part of my week? Watching someone's face when a broken thing works again. That is why I tinker. For that face.$h
dialogue.Sun8: I'm glad the Merchant and the Demolitionist did not run me out of town when I showed up. It could have gone very differently. I owe this valley a lot.$s
dialogue.Mon2: Oh, hello. Mind the sparks near the anvil. They bite.
dialogue.Wed2: Careful with that bucket, @. It holds quenching water and I would hate to see you boil your boots.$h
dialogue.Sat2: Morning market is busy today. Everyone wants their hoes sharpened before the planting rush.
dialogue.Sun2: Oh, it's you. Good. I was about to start hammering and I'd rather you didn't get a headache from it.$h
dialogue.Thu6: You have a good eye for quality, @. The bars you brought me were clean and straight. That is rare.$h
dialogue.Sat6: I've been wondering what you think of the mines these days. I still get a jolt of nerves going down there. Old habits.$s
dialogue.Sun6: I put a little clock on the wall. It is only slightly wrong. The Mechanic says that makes it charming. I say it makes it late.$h
dialogue.Mon10: You are welcome here any time, @. I mean that. Come in when the forge is hot and leave when you've had enough of the noise.$l
dialogue.Wed10: I was going to give you something on your birthday, but I finished it early. You'll find out what it is soon enough.$l
dialogue.Sat10: I'd fight a goblin army for you, @. Not that there are many left. But if there were, I would stand right there beside you.$h
dialogue.spring_Wed: Spring means the mountain thaw brings fresh ore into the mines. I have plenty to do. Good thing I like digging.$h
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer heat turns my forge into an oven. I do not complain. Much.
dialogue.fall_Sat: Fall means the fair is coming, and every tool in town needs sharpening first. Busy, busy.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: Winter nights are the best for the forge. Warm fire, cold windows, and a friend to talk to. That's a fine winter, @.$l
dialogue.fall_15: Halfway through fall already. I have counted my bars twice and both counts agree. I am now a very organized goblin.$h
dialogue.winter_Mon: The ground is frozen, so the mines are quiet. Quiet is good for thinking. I have been thinking about you, @.$l
dialogue.spring_Sun: A spring Sunday. The birds outside are louder than my hammer. I call that a victory for the birds.$h
dialogue.summer_Fri8: Hot nights by the forge with the doors open, the sea breeze coming in. Summer is the time for a cold drink with a good friend.$l

rainy: Rain drumming on the forge roof, @. Puts me in the mood to tinker with clockwork. Nothing beats a rainy afternoon of gears and gossip.$h

situations.eye: The big eye is gone from the sky. Good riddance. I didn't like being watched while I worked, @.$u
situations.evilBoss: One of those horrid worms or brain things finally got what was coming to it. The mines feel a little lighter today.
situations.skeletron: The giant skull fell apart in the dungeon and the Old Man is free! The Clothier nearly wept into his hat. Good news for everybody, @.$h
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is dead. Her honey goes in my cauldron now, I am not wasting a drop of it. Sweet victory, @.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh fell, and now the Hallow is spreading with stronger monsters behind it. Hardmode, @. Time to make better tools.$u
situations.mechs: One of those mechanical bosses got smashed to bits last night. I know those gears well. I'd love a few spares for my bench, but I won't say how I'd come by them.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated. The jungle temple is open, and there are flowers the size of a house in there. I want a sample, @.$u
situations.golem: The stone golem finally came apart in the temple. Gears everywhere. I took a few, and I will be keeping them away from the Mechanic.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is gone. Those celestial pillars glow over the valley now. Pretty, but my compass keeps spinning.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is defeated, @. My ears are still ringing. Whatever fell from the sky, I am keeping a piece of it for the bench.$u
situations.goblins: The goblin army came and went again. Believe me, I know how goblins fight. I helped you beat them, and I am proud of that.$h
situations.pirates: Pirates tried to take the beach last night. The Pirate says he stayed out of it. Mostly. Bring cannons next time.
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion pushed into the valley and got pushed right back out. Their icy armor is a fine material for a tinkerer. Shame it melts so quickly.
situations.martians: Martians in the valley! Ray guns and flying saucers. The Steampunker was thrilled. I was only worried about the crops, @.$u
situations.bloodMoon: The moon was red last night. Not a good sign. Keep your sword sharp and your bombs sharper, @.$u
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark last night. I kept the forge burning the whole time, just in case. Good thing too.$h
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today, which means hammering is for later. I already built a stage for her, @. Don't tell her I cried at the fireworks.

festivals.spring13: Egg Festival! I hid a few tinkered eggs in the grass. They chirp when you find them. Good luck, @.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance! I would love to dance, but I have sooty hands. Maybe next year I'll wash them first.
festivals.summer11: Luau time! I dropped a rusty gear into the community soup. It adds a fine flavor, I promise you.$h
festivals.summer28: The Moonlight Jellies glow on the beach and remind me of the glowing ore veins deep in the caves. Beautiful, @.$h
festivals.fall16: Fair day! I entered my clockwork bird in the contest. It flew for six whole seconds. A triumph.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve. I am not scared of the maze, I have been in goblin caves. But the ghosts are unnerving, and so are those carved pumpkins.$u
festivals.winter8: Ice fishing and snow sculptures. I built a snow cannon and nobody asked me to. It's a classic, @.$h
festivals.winter25: Feast of the Winter Star. I wrapped a gift in old wire for the Merchant. Don't tell them, @.$h

loved.text: Now this is a fine piece! I could build something amazing out of it. Thank you, @.$h

liked.text: Ooh, that's useful. Right into the toolbox it goes.$h

neutral.text: Hm. Decent enough. I'll find a use for it eventually.

disliked.text: Ugh. Take that back, @. I don't need junk cluttering up my forge.$a

hated.text: Get that trash out of my face! I am a tinkerer, not a rubbish bin.$a

help: Oi! Something's sniffing around my forge!
Over here! Bring a hammer, I'm out of patience!
Bit of help here? They've got teeth and no manners!
thanks: Thanks, @. I'd have a few new dents without you.$h
Good work, @. Next time I bring the big hammer, not just my temper.$u
battle: You want my anvil? Come and get it!
Hold the line! Nothing gets past this forge!
Back to your hole, you overgrown rat!
Ha! Goblins are only allowed to be ugly here!
courage.hurt: Got clonked right in the ribs. Give me a day of bandages and coals and I'll be back at the forge. Don't fuss, @.$s

danger.boss: Something huge is loose out there. I'm not chasing it. I'll stay right here and let it come to my forge, @.
danger.invasion: Goblin armies, pirates, whatever they are. They're at the gate. I'll hold the anvil line and not one step back.
danger.pumpkinMoon: Pumpkin Moon. Scarecrows lurking at the edge of the fields. I'll stay by the furnace, thanks.$h
danger.frostMoon: Frost Moon, and the presents are walking. I'd rather be warm behind my forge than chase a gift.$u
danger.eclipse: Solar eclipse. Dark things are dropping out of the sky. Stay near the light, @, and let them come to us.
danger.bloodMoon: Blood moon rising. Bolts on the doors, nails in the boards. Let them try to climb in here.

events.after: Keep your hair away from the sparks, @. It smells terrible when it burns.

steps.say: Oh! @, you walked right into my sparks. Hold still while I check the anvil.$u
Hm. A chipped edge. Nothing a bit of heat won't fix. Hot work keeps a goblin honest, I always say.$h

steps.question: Do you like watching things get fixed?

answers.reply: Good! Then you'll like the next bit, I promise.$h
Hmph. Your loss, then. Bolts and all.$a

steps.say: You seem like the sort who wanders into trouble. Here. Five bars of iron, shaped by my own hands, mostly. Don't drop them in lava.$h

events.after: Wind it up if you ever get bored. It only plays properly on the third try.

steps.say: @! Perfect timing. Come look at this. It's a music box I have been trying to get to play properly.$h
I started it years ago, back when I was still a goblin. Stolen gears, a broken spring, one sad whistle. Nobody would give me a second look.$s
Then a Merchant sold me a proper spring at a fair price, and I have been fixing things ever since. Little by little.$h

steps.question: What did you do before you came here?

answers.reply: Ha! Then you know all about hard work and sore backs.$h
Adventurers break more things than they fix. I'm glad you're on the fixing side now.$h

steps.say: Oh, it works! Listen to that. It sounds like home, @.$h
Keep the box, if you like. Wind it up when the mines get lonely.$h

events.after: The Steampunker says the spring is too loose. I say it is perfect. We're still arguing.

steps.say: Oh! @, and our tinkering friend too. Good, you can both settle an argument for me.$h
The spring is too loose. Honestly, the spring is perfectly loose.
Fine. You are both right, and I am mostly wrong. The spring is a little rusty.$s
Honest answer. Since the goblins left I have been a little lonely. You two are the nicest company I have had in a long time.$l

steps.question: Want to stay for a cup of cider?

answers.reply: Good! Follow me. The cider is by the anvil and I'll fetch the crate.$h
Fine. I'll keep the cider warm. Don't let the Steampunker drink it all.$s

events.after: I'm not sleeping, so I'm polishing. Come by anytime, the door is open.

steps.say: @? Come in, come in. The forge is warm tonight. I couldn't sleep, so I've been polishing things.$s
You know what I kept from the goblin camp? Just one thing. A tin cup my mother bent into a bell shape. Everything else I left behind.$s
When I'm with the valley folks, the cup feels like it's finally mine. Not something I stole. Something I made a home for.$h
Want to know a secret? I hung it by the door. Every time someone walks in, it rings. I'm glad it rings for you, @.$l

steps.question: Do you think I belong here?

answers.reply: Thank you, @. I never said it out loud before, but I'm glad you agree.$l
Honest, at least. Fair enough. I'll earn it the slow way.$s

events.after: Ring that bell if you need me, @. I'll come running, even if I trip on the way.

steps.say: @. Hello, friend. I have something to show you. I've been working on it for a month, so hold still.$h
I melted down the old tin cup and recast it as a bell. Gold this time. Hardly the same thing, but I want you to have a piece of it.$l
Thank you for the ringing at the door, and the company, and for coming by whenever the forge is cold.$l

steps.question: Will you keep it with you?

answers.reply: Then the bell is in good hands. Ring it when you are lost and I'll find you.$l
Nice is enough for me, @. Now stop smiling, I can see it from here.$h

steps.say: Goodnight, @. Don't stay out past the lamplight. The valley is safer with you in it.$h
